subject: Next steps: commercial on-ramp, PO vs card, and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@greengrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Owens <ben.owens@greengrid.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + procurement path options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our call, I wanted to capture a short recap and a few clear next steps so your procurement and finance teams can evaluate options quickly. High-level notes: 

- Primary objective: pilot using Redwood for inference in your anomaly-detection pipeline (100k tokens/day initial).
- Two commercial on-ramps discussed: 1) standard PO / SOW with monthly invoicing, 2) self-serve card payment (faster, no PO) and 3) marketplace listing (AWS Marketplace) as a longer-term option.
- Internal review path you mentioned: legal -> security (questionnaire/SOC2) -> finance -> PO issuance. Ben will own finance side.

Proposed short MAP (mutual action plan):
1) I’ll share a draft SOW and a short T&Cs summary (attached).
2) You run the legal/security questionnaire (we can send an expedited SOC2 packet).
3) Finance confirms PO timeline or opts for card to get started quickly.
4) We stand up a pilot on a hosted Redwood instance; will handoff to deployment/sre as needed.

Can you confirm: which path does finance prefer (PO vs card) for pilots? If PO, what is your typical review SLA (legal/security/finance) so we can map milestones?

Next steps from my side: attach SOW draft and T&Cs summary by end of day. Looping Marcus and Monica on this thread for commercial/legal clarifications.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement path options (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks, Lauren —

Appreciate the succinct MAP. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Finance preference: PO for anything that will be on the books >$5k/month, but they will allow a one-month card trial for evaluation if legal signs off.
- Timeline constraints: legal typically 7-10 business days for standard SOWs, security will want the SOC2 and may have a short Q&A (3–5 business days once they see the packet).
- Marketplace: procurement is open to marketplace if the cadence fits our internal cataloging rules, but that's likely Q3 work for us.

Questions:
1) For the PO path, do you accept our standard redlines or do you require a joint round of edits via DocuSign?
2) If we go card for a month, what are cancellation/auto-renew terms?

Ben — assigning you to confirm finance cadence and PO owner.

Sophie
Sophie Martin
Head of Data Products, GreenGrid Analytics
Sophie.Martin@greengrid.ai | (617) 222-4444

Thanks Sophie — looping in Marcus (commercial lead) and Monica (legal) to address the redline and payment questions. I’ll answer the cancellation question below so you have the quick version for finance.

Quick answers: 
- Card trial: 30-day trial with prorated charge, cancel anytime before day 30 with no further obligation. Auto-renew to card unless a PO is provided and processed by finance.
- PO path: we are typically able to accept customer redlines but need to review major changes that affect liability or data terms. Monica will flag any high-risk items and propose language.

Proposed MAP timeline based on the dates you gave: 
Week 1 (this week): Redwood sends SOW + T&Cs summary (done).
Week 2: GreenGrid legal/security review (7–10 business days).
Week 3: Finance finalizes PO or approves card trial.
Week 4: Pilot starts (1-month pilot).

If PO path is chosen, please share your standard PO template and any required billing contact info; that will help our finance team accelerate net-terms setup.

Monica / Marcus — can you confirm: 1) acceptable turnaround for our side to review customer redlines (we typically target 3 business days for standard edits), and 2) if we need a short commercial exception for pilot pricing or credits, what approvals are required?

Thanks —
Lauren
